question.text: If $A=\frac{1}{3}\left[\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 \\ a & 2 & b\end{array}\right]$ is an orthogonal matrix, then

solution.text:
We know that, if $A$ is an orthogonal matrix, then
$\begin{gathered}
\Rightarrow \quad \ AA^T=I \\
\Rightarrow \\
\Rightarrow \quad\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 2 & 2 \\
2 & 1 & -2 \\
a & 2 & b
\end{array}\right] \cdot \frac{1}{3}\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 2 & a \\
2 & 1 & 2 \\
2 & -2 & b
\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{lll}
1 & 0 & 0 \\
0 & 1 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & 1
\end{array}\right] \\
\Rightarrow\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 2 & 2 \\
2 & 1 & -2 \\
a & 2 & b
\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 2 & a \\
2 & 1 & 2 \\
2 & -2 & b
\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{lll}
9 & 0 & 0 \\
0 & 9 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & 9
\end{array}\right] \\
\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
9 & 0 & a+4+2 b \\
0+4+2 b & 9 & 2 a+2-2 b \\
2 a+2-2 b & a^2+4+b^2
\end{array}\right] \\
\quad=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
9 & 0 & 0 \\
0 & 9 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & 9
\end{array}\right] \\
\Rightarrow \quad a+4+2 b=0 \text { and } 2 a+2-2 b=0 \\
a+2 b=-4 \ldots(i)\\
a-b=-1 \ldots(ii)
\end{gathered}$
By solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$a=-2, b=-1$
